item.title: Kotlin Multiplatform in 2026: Sharing Code Between Android and iOS Without Compromise
item.description: I’ve shipped the same login screen twice — once in Kotlin for Android, once in Swift for iOS — more times than I’d like to admit. Same validation rules, same API calls, same retry logic, written twice, tested twice, and inevitably drifting apart the moment one platform gets a bugfix the other doesn’t. Kotlin Multiplatform was supposed to fix that, and for a long time it felt like a promising side project more than a real answer.

item.title: Jetpack Compose Goes Compose-First in 2026: What Android Developers Need to Know
item.description: I spent last week migrating a legacy RecyclerView screen to Compose, and about halfway through I realized I wasn’t doing it because I felt like it anymore — I was doing it because Google just told the entire Android ecosystem that Views is no longer where new work happens. That’s a bigger deal than another Compose point release, so I want to walk through what actually changed at I/O 2026, what’s new in Compose 1.
